x: Ted Smith had an off day, but Eglington and Ferguson showed improved form. Charlie Speechley, our evergreen at sixty-five years of age, again showed he can still show the youngsters how.

However this was partly compensated for by the "A" team consisting of Hall, Checkley, Eglington and Haynes taking 2nd place in the handicap team race, thus once again proving that our younger members were showing improvement.

All the handicap team prizes stopped over our side of the water as Surrey W.C. took 1st place, our "B" team (Demmon, Middleton Wilson,Doubleday) were 2nd and the "A" Team (Hall,Checkley,Eglington McMullen) were 3rd.
All the good peerformances were too numerous to give in detail, but briefly Hall, Phillips, Demmon, Middleton, Eglington Newson and Scamell all beat the hour and were awarded their 7 miles badges.
The next three places were filled by Surrey and then three more for us - Guilmant, Eglington and Demmon. Scoring 20 a side, we won by 397 points to 423.

Hugh McGreechan was 3rd in the scratch race in 2 hrs. 34mins.44secs., our "A" Team - McGreechan Newson and Eglington - won the handicap team race, the "B" Team - Rolfe Wilson and Doubleday - were 2nd; Bernard Eglington (22.0) won the individual handicap, and Fred Rolfe (28.0) was 2nd in fact it is r…

Bernard Eglington, 13th, missed his by one position. George Beecham gained his first National winning team medal, Hugh McGreechan the Sydney Bayliss Cup and Bob Newson his first (2nd Class) National Standard medal.

John Knifton was 24th in Section A Barnes, Belderson, Beecham and Keown, 6th 7th 30th and 32nd respectively in Section B; Eglington, Cameron, McLennan, Duncan,Wilson and Doubleday between 18 and 62 in Section C; Bushman, East and Logan 14th,15th and 34th in Section D.
